prayerExcerpt.en-US: Sufferings were to the martyrs the most distinguishing mercy, extraordinary graces, and sources of the greatest crowns and glory.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Os sofrimentos foram para os mártires a mais distinta misericórdia, graças extraordinárias, e fontes das maiores coroas e glória.

meta.face: Two clearly different young Romans with fair-olive skin. TIBURTIUS (left), about twenty-two, BEARDLESS: a SQUARE face with a WIDE, flat forehead and a BROAD, BLUNT jaw — a short, UPTURNED nose, round, lively grey eyes under curved light-brown brows, a wide mouth with a faint smile, thick, wavy chestnut hair to the ears. SUSANNA (right), about twenty: a LONG, NARROW face — a high forehead, a long, fine, gently AQUILINE nose, HEAVY-LIDDED dark almond eyes under straight dark brows, narrow cheeks, a small, closed mouth, a small POINTED chin; black hair parted in the centre under the veil; her gaze lowered. Not the soft oval of the virgin martyrs (agnes, cecilia).
meta.basis: No likeness survives of either. Tiburtius's cult is certain (his tomb ad Duas Lauros on the Via Labicana, praised by Damasus); Susanna is commemorated through the titular church named for her. The book tells both and its engraving shows them side by side; the faces are ours.
